# Oliviacode

> Oliviacode is an independent, MIT-licensed desktop client for OpenCode. It bundles no
> model provider, no base URL and no credential: you connect a provider or you do not.
> Windows, macOS and Linux. Current release: 2.2.7.

Oliviacode is a shell, not a service. The agent engine is OpenCode; this project supplies
the window, the session store and the egress layer. Nothing in it names an official or
endorsed provider, and nothing telephones home.

## Canonical links

- [Source repository](https://github.com/9562295450/Oliviacode)
- [Project site](https://9562295450.github.io/Oliviacode/)

- [Checksums and VirusTotal results](https://9562295450.github.io/Oliviacode/checksums.html)
- [Installer SHA-256 list](https://github.com/9562295450/Oliviacode/releases/download/v2.2.7/SHA256SUMS.txt)

## What it does

- Sessions and projects stored locally in SQLite under the user profile; fork, move and
  compact from the UI.
- Egress lanes: Direct, Cloudflare WARP, Tor and HTTP proxy. A rotation is recorded only
  after the provider endpoint reports the new address, so a silent fallback is recorded
  as a failure rather than as success. Lanes fail independently; auto-recover is off by
  default.
- MCP servers connect at launch and their tools are callable from the composer.
- Provider-agnostic: any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint, configured by the user.

## What it does not do

- No bundled provider endpoint, API key or default model.
- No analytics, telemetry or account system.
- No affiliation with, endorsement by, or support commitment from the OpenCode project.

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11 x64, macOS 14+ (arm64 or x64), or Linux x64 (AppImage, deb, rpm).
- A provider endpoint, if you want model replies. The app opens without one.

## Licence

MIT. Source and releases are public; the app is built from that source by its own
release workflow.
